Issued at 218 AM MDT Sun Sep 13 2026

Some people who read my discussions know that I like the reference 
old song lyrics to compare to the weather. And today's reference is 
another 1980s song, Madonna's second hit, "Borderline". In the song, 
she talks about pushing her love over the borderline. In the 
weather, the question is whether or not the weather can cross the 
borderline into needing highlights. And we have two of these 
dilemmas this morning. 

The borderline conditions are not today for the most part though. 
Today will be a warm late summer / early fall day across the 
area. An approaching cold front and a trough axis will tighten 
the pressure gradient across the area, and bring a breezy to 
windy afternoon across the area. Temperatures East of the Divide
will rise well into the 80s, with a few of the warmer spots 
possibly getting close to 90. As for fire weather, critical fire
weather does not look likely as dew points will be rising ahead
of the front, although some locations will see isolated fire 
weather at times this afternoon. As for the chance of 
precipitation, the morning looks generally dry. The one fly in 
the ointment is the European model does have some light showers 
over the far northern and eastern areas before noon. However, 
this model is the outlier and even the this model is further 
east than the 12Z run. So, we kept the forecast dry for now, but
a 10 percent chance of a shower is still possible. A few 
showers and thunderstorms will break out this afternoon, but the
bulk of the activity should hold off until this evening.

All guidance shows a chance of showers tonight, with the best chance 
in southeastern portions of the area. Many areas will have a chance 
though. There is still disagreement in rainfall amounts though, 
especially with the convective nature of the precipitation. As for 
flooding potential, there could be some locally heavy rain but with 
strong steering flow, showers and storms will be moving so the 
threat looks minimal. This is where we reach the first borderline 
situation. And this is for the potential for high wind. We do have 
one of the indications for high wind across portions of the area, we 
do have some 700 millibar winds of 50 knots. There will also be a 
decent jet streak moving in, around 100 knots this evening. There 
are some indications against it though. For one, it looks like a 
brief period of higher wind aloft, generally less than 6 hours. 
Also, ensemble guidance, both the HREF and NBM ensembles, gives less 
than 1 in 3 chance of wind gusts over 55 mph except in the 
mountains. The one location I am most concerned about is the Cody 
Foothills, where there are some indications of a possible mountain 
wave or gap flow, especially between midnight and 5 am. The best 
chance of this would be near Clark, where criteria is higher. We 
will hold off on any wind highlights for now and let the day shift 
take another look. Any showers should end by shortly after sunrise 
on Monday.

Then we move to Monday, where we have our other situation of 
borderline highlights. The 700 millibar wind will remain strong, but 
will gradually decrease through the day as the jet streak moves 
away. The borderline situation is potential Fire Weather. Areas like 
Natrona and Sweetwater County will have the wind, with a greater 
than 4 out of 5 chance of wind gusts over 30 mph through the day. 
Humidity looks borderline though. Further west in Fremont County, 
the humidity will be plenty low. However, wind looks more borderline 
with only a 1 out of 2 chance of wind gusts over 30 mph. Also, if 
there is a decent amount of rain in Natrona County, it could wet the 
fuels. However, it has been very dry. And, with thinking that fire 
weather is the greater threat than high wind, we have issued a Fire 
Weather watch for the above mentioned areas. It will also be a 
cooler day behind the front, with high temperatures 10 to 15 degrees 
less than on Sunday.

Tuesday looks like a dry and seasonable day across most of the
area with less wind. A bit of moisture may come far enough 
north for another chance of a shower or thunderstorm across 
Sweetwater County. And, much like yesterday. Wednesday into next
weekend remains in flux with a lot of uncertainty. The main 
driver this far out will be an upper level low that will be 
located over the Pacific Northwest on Wednesday. The models 
continue to struggle with its movement, especially the European 
which has trended slower and further north. At this point, it 
looks like there will be a chance of showers and thunderstorms 
each day from Wednesday through Friday. However, confidence in 
picking a more active day and especially pinpointing the most 
numerous showers remains very low. So the forecast is subject to
change in the extended portion of the forecast. And with the 
southwest flow ahead of the low, temperatures should rebound to 
above normal levels once again for later in the week.
